rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī places the passage after the deniers’ prideful rejection of resurrection, contrasting that posture with reflection on humanity’s humble origin.
rows.anchor: ولما تقدم في القيامة إخباره تعالى عن حال منكري البعث عنادا واستكبارا وتعاميا عن النظر والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator formed varied bones, joints, tendons, and ligaments, specifying their shapes and counts so the body can move and remain sound.
rows.anchor: وقدرها بمقادير وأشكال مختلفة , فمنها صغير وكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distinct senses and organs serve precise purposes: eyes convey images, ears gather sound, the nose detects scents, teeth divide food, and the tongue expresses thought.
rows.anchor: ففتح العين ورتب طبقاتها وأحسن شكلها ولونها وأحكمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Internal organs divide the work of digestion and circulation; the entire intricate body begins as a tiny drop in three layers of darkness, proving its unseen Maker.
rows.anchor: وكان مبدأ ذلك كله النطفة على صغرها في داخل الرحمن في ظلمات ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People marvel at a fine design on a wall yet overlook the Creator of the far greater wonders in themselves and others.
rows.anchor: فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأبهر برهانه , فيالله العجب ممن يرى نقشا حسنا على جدار فيتعجب من حسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding outward and inward sin requires avoiding each kind; if unbelievers invite the Prophet to something involving neither sin nor disbelief, he may accept.
rows.anchor: وأفهم ترتيب النهي على الوصفين أنه إذا دعاه الكفار إلى ما لا يتعلق به إثم ولا كفر جاز له قبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unhindered remembrance of God is the remedy for spiritual harm and precedes worship, since knowing God is worship’s aim and thought joined to worship is its highest form.
rows.anchor: والذكر مقدم على كل عبادة وإن وضع العباد لما كان طلبا للتواصل إلى نيل معرفة الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning remembrance follows waking, a minor death, and recalls resurrection; evening remembrance recalls the world’s ending, while naming both times signals continual remembrance.
rows.anchor: عند قيامك من منامك الذي هو الموتة الصغرى وتذكر أنه يحيي الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God’s name may command prayer, the best bodily worship because it joins tongue, heart, and limbs in ordered acts that affirm the Creator’s existence and oneness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أمرا بالصلاة لأنها أفضل الأعمال البدنية لأنها أعظم الذكر لأنها ذكر اللسان والجنان والأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading prescribes dawn and afternoon prayers, which were the only prayers commanded early in Islam and were then two cycles each.
rows.anchor: فيكون هذاعلى هذا أمراص بصلاتي الصبح والعصر , فإنه لم يكن أمر في اول الإسلام بغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command includes dawn, noon, and afternoon, since the broad term for evening covers the latter two; other prayers are included in the following phrase.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أمرا بصلاتي الصبح والظهر والعصر فإن الأصيل يتناول وقتيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is a dark covering that permits rest from work; day reveals what night hid and provides time for movement and earning a livelihood.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر اللباس أولا دليلا على حذف ضده ثانيا والمعاش ثاينا دليلا على حذف ضده أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God built seven strong, perfectly joined heavens above all directions, untouched by ages until He brings about what He has decreed.
rows.anchor: { فوقكم } أي عاما لجميع جهة الفوق , وهي عبارة تدل على الإحاطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blazing, intensely hot lamp is the sun; the word evokes a jewel shining and an ember burning.
rows.anchor: { سراجا } أي نجما منيرا جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muʿṣirāt are clouds heavy with water and close to being driven by winds into rain, which cools the sun’s heat and enables food and drink.
rows.anchor: أي السحائب التي أثقلت بالماء فشارفت أن يعرصها الرياح فتمطر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ defines a muʿṣir cloud as one that has gathered rain but does not yet rain, comparing it to a girl nearing menstruation without having begun.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : المعصر , السحابة التي تتحلى بالمطر ولا تمطر كالمرأة المعصرة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī understands muʿṣirāt as clouds approaching rainfall, like a woman approaching menstruation.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي : السحائب التي دنت أن تمطر كالمعصرة التي دنت من الحيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thajjāj describes abundant water pouring in successive streams; both the transitive and reflexive forms are used for pouring.
rows.anchor: أي منصبا بكثرة يتبع بعضه بعضا , يقال : ثجه وثج بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain brings out staple grains first, such as wheat and barley, then other vegetation for enjoyment and animal fodder.
rows.anchor: أي نجما ذا حب هو مقصوده لأنه يقتاته العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alfāf means gardens whose trees are packed closely together; he derives this from the abundance of water and explains the plural form.
rows.anchor: أي ملتفة الأشجار مجتمعة بعضها إلى بعض من شدة الري

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that alfāf may be a plural of a plural: a garden is lafāʾ, its plural lif, and the plural of lif is alfāf.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وقيل : هو جمع الجمع , يقال : جنة لفاء , وجمعها لف بضم اللام , وجمع الجمع ألفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky, earth, rain, and plants resemble a reproductive pair: sky is male, earth female, water semen, and vegetation their offspring; springs and pools are implied.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك أشبه شيء بما يتولد بين الزوجين من الأولاد , فالسماء كالزوج والأرض كالمرأة , والماء كالمني

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says every sign just mentioned is more astonishing than resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : وكل من هذا الذي ذكر أعجب من البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of power and wisdom establish divine oneness, stirring obedient believers to long for God and wrongdoers to fear meeting Him.
rows.anchor: فدل قطعا على الوحدانية لأنه لو كان التعدد لم تكن الحكمة ولم تتم القدرة , فأثمر المحبة لمن اتصف بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision is the great announcement and a fixed terminus in God’s knowledge, when creation is gathered and every ambiguity is settled by delivering the wronged from the oppressor.
rows.anchor: يفصل فيه بين كل ملبس فصلا لا شبهة فيه ويؤدخ للمظلوم من الظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is explained as the second blast of resurrection, blown by a permitted blower into a trumpet described as immense and made of light.
rows.anchor: وهو قرن من نور على ما قيل سعته أعظم ما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rising, people return alive with their original bodies intact; God gathers and recomposes them as easily as He first created people from a drop and Adam from soil.
rows.anchor: لا تفقدون من أعضائكم وجلودكم وأشعاركم وأظفاركم وألوانكم الأصلية شيئا يجمعكم من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afwājan means nations, companies, and groups who hurry on foot, each community following its imam.
rows.anchor: أي أمما وزمرا وجماعات مشاة مسرعين كل أمة بإمامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.
rows.anchor: مقصودها بيان أواخر أمر الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Nāziʿāt points to angels extracting souls and then the account of Pharaoh and Moses; al-Sāhirah and al-Ṭāmmah also fit the oath and the surah’s flow.
rows.anchor: وصور ذلك بنزع الأرواح بأيدي الملائكة الكرام ، ثم أمر فرعون اللعين وموسى عليه السلام ، واسمها النازعات واضح في ذلك المرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God manifest and hidden, the knowing King, universally generous in mercy and especially completing His favor for His allies in the Abode of Peace.
rows.anchor: الظاهر الباطن الملك العلام { الرحمن } الذيي عم بالإنعام { الرحيم } الذي خص أهل ولايته بالتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day recur as daily demonstrations of resurrection, since restoring life is no harder than creating humanity from nothing.
rows.anchor: ولما كان كل من ذلك يدل على القدرة على البعث لأنه إيجاد ما هو أشد من خلق الآدمي من عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night darkens when the sun disappears and Earth’s shadow covers what it illuminated; the verse’s ellipsis pairs darkening with omitted brightness and dawn with omitted darkness.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : دل ب ( أغطش ) على ( أضاء ) وبإخراج الضحى على إخفاء الضياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth was created before the heavens but spread and made habitable afterward; the preposition is omitted to convey the duration of its spreading.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المراد استغراق الزمان باستمرار الدحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth’s water comes from within it, as its possessive attribution indicates; its pasture includes what is grazed, its place, and its season.
rows.anchor: بتفجير العيون , وإضافته إليها دليل على أنه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fixed the mountains like anchors that stabilize Earth as anchors stabilize a ship.
rows.anchor: أي أثبتها وأقرها ومع كونها ثابتة لا تتحول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity and livestock enjoy Earth’s provisions, and the repeated cycle of consuming and restoring what is needed illustrates continual renewal and resurrection.
rows.anchor: تتمتعون بما فيها من المنافع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-ṭāmmah al-kubrā as the overwhelming, supreme calamity.
rows.anchor: أي الداهية الدهياء التي تطم أي تعلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apodosis of idhā is omitted and understood as people being divided into the wretched and the blessed.
rows.anchor: والعامل في ( إذا ) محذوف تقديره : فصل الناس إلى شقي وسعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human will recall every good and evil deed in the written record; mentioning remembrance stresses the terror of the coming reckoning.
rows.anchor: أي عمل كله من خير وشر لأنه يراه في صحيفة أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is displayed openly to anyone, and the wording leaves its exhibitor unstated because the terrifying fact is the display itself.
rows.anchor: لأن الهائل مطلق تبريزها لا كونه من معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressor prefers immediate worldly life over the unseen afterlife, behaves like an animal limited to present things, and neglects worship and self-discipline.
rows.anchor: بأن جعل أثر العاجلة الدنية لحضورها عنده أعظم من أثر الآخرة العليا لغيابها

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran grammatical analysis supplies an omitted pronoun after hiya in the phrase meaning that Hell is the abode for the transgressor.
rows.anchor: هذا مذهب البصريين أن الضمير محذوف

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufan analysis makes the definite article al stand in for the omitted pronoun, an analysis Abū Ḥayyān attributes to them.
rows.anchor: وعند الكوفيين أن ( أل ) نائب عن الضمير قاله أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of standing before the Lord means fearing the encounter or its place and time, through awareness of His kindness and majesty; such fear presupposes belief in resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي قيامه بين يدي المحسن إليه عند تذكر إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul must be restrained from every desire, since the Fire is surrounded by appetites and religious law opposes what the lower self wants.
rows.anchor: أي كل ما تهواه فإنه لا جر إلى خير لأن النار حفت بالشهوات

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī defines blameworthy desire as appetite that conflicts with religious commands.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : والهوى هو الشهوة المذمومة المخالفة لأوامر الشرع

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd says that when the self opposes its desire, its illness becomes its cure.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد : إذا خالفت النفس هواها صار داؤها دواءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical arrangement uses transgression to imply the opposite of restraint and restraint to imply rejection of worldly preference.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : أتى بطغى دليلا على ضده ثانيا , وبالنهي عن الهوى ثانيا دلالة على إيثار الدنيا أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise alone is the watchful believer’s final home and reward.
rows.anchor: أي البستان الجامع لكل ما يشتهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh repeatedly ask mockingly when the Resurrection will occur, with marsā meaning its setting, occurrence, or establishment.
rows.anchor: أي قريش على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار سؤال استهزاء وإنكار واستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks why the Prophet is expected to know its timing; even an answer would not help, though his compassion for their conversion might make him wish to reply.
rows.anchor: وكان من المعلوم أنه يقول : إنهم ليسألونني وربما تحركت نفسه الشريفة صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى إجابتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All knowledge and affairs of the Hour end with God, and the Prophet was not commissioned to determine its exact time.
rows.anchor: أي منتهى علمها وجميع أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s mission is to warn those capable of fearing the Hour, not to date it; concealing its time increases the receptive person’s fear, while the heedless become more reckless.
rows.anchor: فما أرسلناك إلا للإنذار بها لا للإعلام بوقتها , فإن النافع الأول دون الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those without fear receive only the outward form of a warning and gain no benefit from it, whereas the fearful understand and act on it.
rows.anchor: فكان كأنه لم يحصل له الإنذار , ولهذا المعنى أضاف إشارة إلى أنه عريق في إنذار من يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Hour, people will think their stay in the world and graves lasted only part of a day: from noon to sunset, or from morning until noon.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا وفي القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison belittles worldly time against the limitless afterlife; the Prophet likens this world’s share to a finger dipped in the sea and withdrawn.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعبير لنا بما نحسه تقريبا لعقولنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers give differing estimates of their stay, but the truth is that their past seems like a brief hour beside the endless future they face.
rows.anchor: على أن الكفار أيضا يستقصرون مدة لبثهم , فكأنهم أصناف : بعضهم يقول : إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison recalls the judgment scene where people say they stayed only an hour, or answer that they remained a day or part of one and defer to the counters.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah closes by returning from resurrection to its opening, then connects to the next surah through fear and remembrance.
rows.anchor: فقد رجع آخرها بالقيامة على أولها , والتف مفصلها بنزع الأنفس اللوامة على موصلها , واتصلت بأول ما بعدها من جهة الخشية والتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that some answer “a day or part of a day” is linked to the question about years in al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم اسأل العادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
rows.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luxury and self-sufficiency signal rejection and readiness for disbelief and wrongdoing; affliction can purify, humble, and soften hearts, so the more deeply tried are more receptive to fear.
rows.anchor: الاستغناء والترف أمارة الإعراض وعدم القابلية والتهيؤ للكفر والفجور ، وإلى أن المصائب أمارة للطهارة والإقبال واستكانة القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name ʿAbasa points to the surah’s lesson, while al-Ṣākhkhah and al-Bākhkhah evoke the blast’s destructive force.
rows.anchor: واسمها عبس هو الدال على ذلك بتأمل آياته وتدبر فواصله وغاياته ، وكذا الصاخة النافخة بشرها وشررها والباخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as powerful and wise, universally granting existence and guidance, and completing His favor specifically for His allies.
rows.anchor: الذي له القدرة البالغة والحكمة الباهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annual cycle of pasture withering, becoming soil, and returning through rain and growth mirrors resurrection and confirms the earlier promise to raise the dead.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك مثل إحياء الموتى سواء , فتحقق لذلك ما تقدم من أمر الإنشار بعد الإقبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After eating from the forbidden tree, Adam was expelled from Paradise to an intermediate abode, neither Paradise nor Fire, bearing signs of both.
rows.anchor: فلما أكل منها أخرجه من الجنة فسبجنه في دار ليست بجنة ولا نار ولا غيرهما بل هي ممن ممتزج الدارين وكالبرزخ بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unavoidable Hour is creation’s purpose: people were entrusted with worldly blessings, failed to thank them, and must answer for their stewardship.
rows.anchor: لأنها سر الكون فإن فيها حساب الذين استخلفوا في هذا الوجود وأفيضت عليهم النعم التي أودعها فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣākhkhah is the deafening cry of resurrection, striking ears with such force that they nearly become deaf and must attend to it.
rows.anchor: الصرخة العظيمة التي يبالغ في إسماع الأسماع بها حتى تكاد تصمها لشدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is appositional to the Hour’s coming and indicates its answer: everyone becomes wholly occupied with himself, unable to attend to anyone else.
rows.anchor: قال مبدلا من ( إذا ) ما يدل على جوابها من نحو : اشتغل كل بنفسه ولم يكن عنده فراغ ما لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a wife is the closest companion and most deeply attached to the heart, a person would defend her in hardship.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الزوجة التي هي أهل لأن تصحب ألصق بالفؤاد وأعرق في الوداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife is especially close to the heart, while sons and daughters inspire intense love, confidences, and counsel and consume a parent’s livelihood and lifetime.
rows.anchor: ولما كان للوالد إلى الولد من المحبة والعاطفة والإباحة بالسر والمشاورة في الأمر ما ليس لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person has an affair sufficient to occupy him, fearing that relatives in their distress will demand rights he neglected.
rows.anchor: ويخاف أن يطالبوه لما هم فيه من الكرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed faces shine, smile, and rejoice at angelic glad tidings; Ibn Umm Maktūm’s steadfast banner-bearing at al-Qādisiyyah exemplifies fear of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وهي بيضاء نيره بما يرى من تبشير الملائكة , وذلك بما كانت فيه في الدنيا من عبوس الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched faces bear dust, gloom, and darkness from hardship, terror, and their past heedless amusement and security from punishment.
rows.anchor: أي كدورة وسواد وظلمة ضد الإسفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ellipsis pairs bright, joyful faces with fear and terror, and dusty faces with whiteness and light, showing relief and hardship as motives for hope and warning.
rows.anchor: ذكر الإسفار والبشر أولا يدل على الخوف والذعر ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelieving and flagrantly wicked are marked by both dust and gloom; the surah’s ending returns to whom one should avoid and whom one should welcome.
rows.anchor: فقد عاد آخرها على أولها فيمن يستحق الإعراض عنه ومن يستحق الإقبال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Takwīr threatens the Day of Judgment as the climactic display of divine majesty and warns those who reject the Qur’an, a reminder preserved in honored, pure pages by angelic scribes.
rows.anchor: مقصودها التهديد الشديد بيوم الوعيد الذي هو محط الرحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trusted heavenly messenger and the Prophet’s known integrity establish the revelation’s truth; its reminders from people and the cosmos suffice for certainty.
rows.anchor: والدلالة على حقية كونه كذلك بأن السفير به أمين في الملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Takwīr points to the opening sign and the surah’s oath, response, and eloquent argument; the basmala names God as sovereign, universally merciful, and specially generous to His beloved.
rows.anchor: واسمها التكوير أدل ما فيها على ذلك بتأمل الظرف وجوابه وما فيه من بديع القول وصوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Takwīr threatens the climactic Day of Judgment and chastises Qur’an deniers; the Qur’an is a reminder in honored, pure pages delivered by trusted angels.
rows.anchor: مقصودها التهديد الشديد بيوم الوعيد الذي هو محط الرحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angelic envoy is trustworthy and the human messenger is beyond accusation; the revelation’s signs in people and the cosmos prove it true.
rows.anchor: والدلالة على حقية كونه كذلك بأن السفير به أمين في الملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title reflects the opening cosmic sign and the surah’s oath and response; the basmala describes God’s universal mercy and special favor to His allies.
rows.anchor: واسمها التكوير أدل ما فيها على ذلك بتأمل الظرف وجوابه وما فيه من بديع القول وصوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic signs in al-Takwīr precede the flight from relatives in ʿAbasa, so the opening of this surah signals the Hour and answers when it will come.
rows.anchor: ووقوع تكوير الشمس وانكدار النجوم وتسيير الجبال وتعطيل العشار كل ذلك متقدم على فرار المرء من أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After associating disgrace with the verse about humanity’s ingratitude, Biqāʿī says the gravest denial after shirk is rejecting the truth, especially the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وأعظمه التكذيب بالقرآن , وذلك التكذيب هو الذي جمع الخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s ordering of judgments, rulings, and knowledge is beyond human capacity and miraculous, so denying it brings the denier complete disgrace.
rows.anchor: لما له من الرونق والجمع للحكم والأحكام والمعارف التي لا يقدر على جمعها على ذلك الوجه وترتيبها ذلك الترتيب إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the opening as declining to swear because the Qur’an’s truth is already manifest and needs no oath.
rows.anchor: أي لأجل حقية القرآن لأن الأمر فيه غنى عن قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khunnas are stars whose rising lags behind the sun and which disappear in daylight; people wrongly attributed rain and mercy to these planets.
rows.anchor: أي الكواكب التي يتأخر طلوعها عن طولع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the wandering planets as Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وهي القمر فعطارد فالزهرة فالشمس فالمريخ فالمشتري فزحل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s mnemonic orders the planets from Saturn down to the Moon, illustrating the sequence just given.
rows.anchor: وقد نظمها بعضهم متدليا فقال : زحل اشترى مريخه من شمسه فتزهرت لعطارد الأقمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jawār al-kunnas are orbiting planets that hide beneath the sun’s brightness by day; the image is compared to wild animals entering their dens.
rows.anchor: أي السيارة التي تختفي وتغيب بالنهار تحت ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says higher planets hide behind lower planets at conjunction, like gazelles concealed in their lairs.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي : يكنس ويستتر العلوي منها بالسفلي عند القرانات كما تستتر الظباء في الكناس

rows.speaker: قتادة وعلي
rows.claim: Qatāda, with the same view also transmitted from ʿAlī, says the stars travel at night and disappear by day.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : تسير بالليل وتخنس بالنهار فتخفى ولا ترى , وروي ذلك أيضا عن علي

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī gives the roots: khunūs is retreating backward, and kunūs is returning to a shelter or lair.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وأصل الخنوس الرجوع إلى وراء والكنوس أن تأوي إلى مكانسها

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī interprets the stars’ hiding as their setting.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري : إن ذلك غروبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the heavenly bodies are useful and impressive, their disappearance and obscured light are defects; the Qur’an is free of such weakness and surpasses all speech.
rows.anchor: وإنما نفى الإقسام بها لأنها وإن كانت عظيمة في أنفسها بما ناط بها سبحانه من المصالح وأنتم تعظمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is the setting where stars emerge as its darkness gathers and deepens after disappearing in daylight.
rows.anchor: أي الذي هو محل ظهور النجوم وزوال خنوسها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Unattributed readings take ʿasʿasa to mean that night departs, darkens, reaches its midpoint, or ends; the cognate verb also carries the sense.
rows.anchor: معناه أدبر , وقيل : أظلم , وقيل : انتصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical ellipsis mentions the stars’ retreat and concealment to imply their appearance, then mentions night to imply the omitted day.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر خنوس الكواكب وكنوسها أولا يفهم ظهورها ثانيا , وذكر الليل ثانيا يفهم حذف النهار أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The morning breathes by shining and spreading its gentle light, dispelling night after night has arrived and departed.
rows.anchor: أي أضاء وأقبل روحه ونسيمه , وأنسه ونعيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even dawn’s light and pleasure pale beside the Qur’an’s light and spiritual delight; the sun’s heat erases morning’s coolness, but nothing erases the Qur’an’s sacred refreshment.
rows.anchor: يتضاءل عن نور القرآن , وما فيه من النعيم والرضوان , ( وأين الثريا من يد المتناول )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noble messenger in this verse is Gabriel, sent as an intermediary to the finest human messenger because ordinary humans cannot bear direct angelic reception.
rows.anchor: وهو جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام نحن أرسلناه به إلى خير خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the revelation the messenger’s speech means Gabriel voiced and conveyed it; in truth it is God’s speech, not an independent composition by the envoy.
rows.anchor: والذي أوحاه وإن كان قوله لكونه نطق به وبلغه من غير مشاركة شيطان ولا غيره هو قول الله من غير شك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger’s complete nobility and moral excellence ensure that he transmits the message exactly, without altering or neglecting it.
rows.anchor: فهو جواد شريف النفس ظاهر عليه معالي الأخلاق بريء من أن يلم شيء من اللوم بساحته , فلذلك هو يفيض الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title al-Inshiqāq points to the opening cosmic sign, while the basmala invokes divine majesty, universal mercy, and completed favor for God’s allies.
rows.anchor: واسمها الانشقاق أدل دليل على ذلك بتأمل الظرف وجوابه الدلال على الناقد البصير وحسابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky will split and open after the dead rise; its perfect obedience is now disputed by deniers who attribute effects to nature or stars, but the event will remove their doubts.
rows.anchor: أي كانت شديدة الاستماع والطواعية والانقياد على أتم وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is made to submit because every created thing is rightly bound to obey its Lord, both at its beginning and at its end.
rows.anchor: فهي حقيقة به لأنها مربوبة له سبحانه , وكل مربوب فهو حقيق بالانقياد لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth will be stretched like leather, widened after becoming level, and cast out its buried wealth and dead until empty, as if deliberately shedding them.
rows.anchor: أي بسطت بسط الأديم ومطت فامتطت فزيد في سعتها جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth’s casting out and emptying happen by the Creator’s command, not by its own power; repeating idhā highlights the immense power in each event.
rows.anchor: فعلت فيه كله فعل السميع المجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two conditional openings have an obvious omitted answer: every person will be judged for all their striving, with disbelievers repaid and Muslims rewarded.
rows.anchor: والجواب محذوف _ لأنه في غاية الانكشاف بما دل عليه المقام مع ما تقدم من المطففين وما قبلها من السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī treats the judgment as unmistakable from the context of al-Muṭaffifīn and the preceding surahs, making the conditional passage’s omitted answer clear.
rows.anchor: بما دل عليه المقام مع ما تقدم من المطففين وما قبلها من السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is like servants presented to a king: their toil can be accepted or rejected, so the outcome follows the quality of their work.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من المعلوم أن عبيد الملك إذا عرضوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with the sky’s splitting and Earth’s stretching introduces judgment and the distribution of books, completing the earlier account of their writing and preservation.
rows.anchor: وافتتحت السورة بذكر انشقاق السماء ومد الأرض وإلقائها ما فيها وتحليها تعريفا بهذا اليوم العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular address treats humanity as a kind before turning to every individual; receiving one’s record in the right hand marks acceptance as a believer and obedient servant.
rows.anchor: فمن كان مقبولا أعطي كتاب حسناته بيمينه لأنه كان في الدنيا من أهل اليمين أي الدين المرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejected person receives the record from behind, a sign of following a false religion without the Owner’s permission.
rows.anchor: ومن كان مردودا أعطي كتابه بشماله لأنه كان في الدنيا مع أهل الشمال وهو الدين الباطل الذي يعمل من غير إذن المالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer receives an easy account because he previously held himself accountable; good deeds are accepted and bad deeds forgiven, apart from lapses of forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: أي سهلا لا يناقض فيه لأنه كان سحاب نفسه فلا يقع له المخالفة إلا ذهولا
